description: A pure CALCULATION node — turn point MATRICES into graph JSON. This is the bridge out of the matrix chain: an N×2 matrix has positions but no connectivity, a graph has edges. Wire the result into Network to draw it.
instructions:
A value-only node: one or two point matrices in, a graph as JSON out. It has no geometry input or output and draws nothing itself — wire `val-graph` into a Network node (or Merge Graph / Graph Reduce / Mitered Join) to see it.

WHY IT EXISTS: every matrix node speaks `[[x,y],…]`, which carries positions but no edges. Network needs { nodes: [{id,x,y}], edges: [{from_node_id,to_node_id}] }. This node adds the connectivity.

INPUTS: wire point lists into valin-a and valin-b — `val-points` from Space Geometry / Polygon / Vertices, or any N×2 `val-matrix` from the Matrix and Vector nodes.

MODES:
• Pairs (A → B) — one edge per row, from A[i] to B[i]. Both inputs required, and the row count is the shorter of the two. This is the mode for drawing a family of rays or spokes (e.g. each polygon vertex to its offset position).
• Ring (closed) — A[0]→A[1]→…→A[n-1]→A[0]. Draws a point list as a closed outline.
• Path (open) — A[0]→A[1]→…→A[n-1], no closing edge.
• Points only — nodes, no edges.

COINCIDENT POINTS MERGE: positions are keyed to the millimetre, so two rows landing on the same spot become ONE graph node. That is what makes converging rays read as a connected skeleton rather than a bundle of separate spokes, and it drops any edge whose two ends have collapsed together.

PER-EDGE THICKNESS: wire an N×1 COLUMN into valin-thickness (metres, row i = edge i — the same row that produced the edge) and every edge carries its own `thickness`. A single scalar broadcasts to all edges; leave it empty and no thickness is written at all. This is how one graph holds a 0.23 m exterior wall and a 0.1 m interior wall at once, instead of needing Set Thickness per family.

EDGE TYPE: the optional Edge type param stamps `type` on every edge produced here — "wall", "door", "window" or "opening". Merge Graph preserves it, so a wall graph, a door graph and a window graph union into ONE graph whose edges stay distinguishable downstream. Mitered Join and Graph to Matrix SKIP `type: "opening"` edges, so use "door" / "window" when the openings should still be stroked.

OUTPUT: `val-graph` plus `val-nodeCount` / `val-edgeCount` (what actually survived the merge). Every parameter is wireable (valin-*).
